main_text.p: Collocatio & tractatio sententiarum in singulis epistolæ partibus.laude atq; gloria moueri folent. Ad tractationem porrò, atq; collocatione quod attinet, quatuor potisimum partib. Conciliatoriæ epistolæ constant: quarum prima Exordium ita est instituendum, vt non vel pudenter, vel prudenter parum aliorū nobis conciliare amore atq; beneuolentiam velle videamur. Itaq; aut scriptionis causas indicabimus: petitas à prædicatione, vel spe egregia humanitatis, beneuolétiæ, auxilij eius ad quê literas damus. li.5.e.4. 9.l.15.e.10. Aut eiusdem intermissæ hactenus rationes exponemus.l.5.e.4. Aut longioris causarū enumerationis Exordia.ὑποδιώξει[?] reiectione vtemur.libr.6.epist.16. Pars altera Propositiones.propositio ἀξιωματικὴ[?] erit petitoria, vt, quâtū quidem amici fert volûtas, nos in suorum album ascribat. libr.5.epist.4.9.lib.6. epist.16.lib.15. epist. 10. Pars tertia confirmatio argumenta continebit, quæ ad nos Confirmationes.amandos atq; promouendos impellere amicum possunt: vt sunt petita ab eius cõfuetudine, studio, amore, beneuolentia, lib.15. epist.10. laude & commendatione doctrinæ, virtutum, aut cæterarum rerum. lib.5. epist.4.9.lib.15. epist.10. Noftra gratitudine & memoria. lib.5.epist.4. Necesfario.lib.5.epist.4. Facili. lib.15.epistol.10.

page.notes: Page 117 of a 16th-century Latin printed book (Conciliatoriis). Doubtful readings: "potisimum" (may be "potissimum"), "instituendum", the Greek words in lines 14 and 16 (marked [?]), and "ὑποδιώξει" in particular. The margin notes' placement is approximate; they are placed beside the lines where they appear. The Greek letters should be checked against the scan.
